🏺

Glaze Search · How to use

A friendly guide with real examples. Every photo, number and recipe below comes from the app itself, run on 2026-11-05. The deeper parts are in yellow 🐇 rabbit hole boxes: skip them on a first read.

1 What it does2 Start it3 The six pages4 Example A: test tiles 5 Examples B–D: vase, bowl, mug6 Words only7 A formula8 All answers 9 What the numbers mean10 Photo + words + formula11 Tips12 Where things are

1 · What the app does

You show it a pot. It tells you what it sees and finds glaze recipes that could make a similar glaze.

📷 What is this pot?From a photo: the glaze colour, the shape and the surface, each with how sure the model is.
🧪 Which recipe makes it?The closest of 7,063 real recipes from Glazy, from words, a colour, the photo or a chemical formula.
🏺 What looks like it?The most similar pots among 12,309 objects cut out of Glazy photos, with ✓ / ✗ for shape, glaze and colour.

Everything runs on your own computer; only the recipe photos are loaded from Glazy's website (internet needed for them).

2 · Start the app

  1. Double-click RUN_GLAZE_SEARCH.bat (in the project folder). A black window opens: keep it open while you use the app; closing it stops the app.
  2. Wait about 30–60 seconds until the window says Glaze recipe model ready and Smart search model ready. The page opens in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:8770.
  3. Use the coloured buttons at the top to move between pages. Your photo and choices stay when you switch.

First time on a new PC: SETUP.bat → DOWNLOAD_DATA.bat → CHECK_DATA.bat → INSTALL_GLAZE_MODEL.bat (with the team's model ZIP), then RUN_GLAZE_SEARCH.bat.

3 · The six pages

Each page has its own colour, and each one does one job.

Four test tiles: the yellow one

Step 1 · 📷 My photo: find the pots and pick the glaze

What you doClick the example (or drop the photo). Click the yellow tile. Switch to 🎨 Pick colour and click on the yellow glaze, not on the bare clay at the bottom.

🐇 Rabbit hole: where do these answers come from?
  • Cutting out: Grounding DINO draws a box around each “ceramic object”, SAM 2.1 traces its exact outline, and CLIP checks it is ceramic (1.00 here; below 0.35 an object is not used by default). That is why a hand or a table is left out (see example C).
  • Colour regions: inside the outline, pixels with similar colour are grouped. This tile has two regions: R1 sand 68 % (the glaze) and R2 warm gray 32 % (the bare clay). Picking with 🎨 makes sure the glaze is used.
  • Shape and surface: Grounding DINO looks for phrases such as “flat rectangular tile” or “mirror-like reflection”; a small trained layer turns that into a probability. Shape test tile 100 % is almost certain. The surface is not: satin 39 %, glossy 31 %, satin-matte 15 %. Glazy says satin-matte, which is only the model's third choice. Surfaces are hard to see in a photo (on 240 test objects the first surface guess was right 45 % of the time, the first shape guess 84 %).

🐇 Rabbit hole: how is the score 0.787 of “Buttercream” made?

Only the parts you gave count. Here that is the photo (weight 0.35) and the colour (0.30). Their weights are scaled to add up to 1: photo 0.35 / 0.65 = 0.54, colour 0.30 / 0.65 = 0.46.

colour part = exp(−ΔE00 / 20) = exp(−2.58 / 20) = 0.879

score = 0.5385 × 0.709 (photo) + 0.4615 × 0.879 (colour) = 0.787

The bars on each card show the same thing: the bar length is the part's own score (0–1), the number is its share of the total.

Why is the tile's own recipe not first? Glazy's photo of “Satin matte base glaze” shows four colours. The photo part compares your yellow tile with the whole recipe photo, so other, all-yellow recipes are closer. Its rank here: not in the top 10. With a one-glaze photo the own recipe does come first (examples C and D).

🐇 Rabbit hole: a match that is not the same colour

Score = 0.40 learned match + 0.40 colour + 0.10 surface + 0.10 cone. For #1: 0.40 × 0.553 + 0.40 × 0.854 + 0.10 × 1 + 0.10 × 1 = 0.763

#3 “Yoko's Leaf Green” is green-gray: ΔE00 12.0, so its colour part is only 0.55 (✗ not the same colour). It still ranks high because its chemistry fits the words best (learned match 0.73) and cone and surface match. That is why the app shows ΔE00 on every card: check it. Below about 5 the colours look alike; above 10 they are different colours.

🐇 Rabbit hole: reading ✓ and ✗, and this search's scores

Each pot is checked against simple rules (this check never changes the order):

criterion (rule)Hit@3Hit@10P@10matching pots in the database
shape same object form: test tile✓✓100 %9,555
glaze same surface group: satin (your object: satin)✓✓30 %4,359
colour within ΔE2000 20 of #AEA86E✓✓90 %9,295
strict shape AND glaze AND colour✓✓20 %2,798
weighted shape 0.20 + glaze 0.45 + colour 0.35nDCG@10 0.70 · nDCG@3 0.76
  • #1 is the tile itself (the photo is in the database): ✓ everything.
  • #2 and #3 are the other tiles of the same photo: same shape and close colour, but their surface label is not satin, so ✗ glaze and ✗ strict.
  • #6 is the mauve tile: ΔE 25.1 is more than 20, so ✗ colour.
  • Hit@3 ✓ means at least one of the first 3 pots matches. P@10 20 % for strict means 2 of the first 10 pots match on all three. nDCG@10 0.70: 1 would be the best possible order.
  • The colour rule uses the colour region the app thinks matters most (#AEA86E). Mark a region important under Your object up close to choose it yourself.

🐇 Rabbit hole: two readers at once

The words are used twice. (1) A rule-based reader finds values: colour → HEX, “^6” → cone 6, “shinyy” → Glossy, “ox” → Oxidation. Those values are scored exactly (match = 1, no match = 0). (2) A trained text model reads the whole sentence and compares it with every recipe. Parts here: words 0.39 · colour 0.33 · cone 0.11 · surface 0.11 · atmosphere 0.06.

On 300 noisy test sentences the top 10 had the right colour + surface + cone 54 % of the time with the text model alone, 55 % with the read values alone and 73 % with both; that is why both are used.

🐇 Rabbit hole: matched or not matched?

Its own recipe came #11. So with Show 10 it is ✗ not in the top 10 (Hit@10 = no), and with Show 20 it is ✓ in the top 20 (Hit@20 = yes). The top 3 are other copper + iron glazes with similar chemistry: a formula finds similar chemistry, not a guaranteed colour (their photos are brown-black and dark green, because firing, thickness and clay change the colour).

On all 1,059 test recipes a formula alone found the right recipe in the top 10 for 33 % of them; random guessing would give 0.9 %. A formula needs at least 3 oxides including a flux (for example CaO, K2O or Na2O); otherwise the app says so and ignores it.

9 · What the numbers mean

NumberIn simple wordsExactly
% on My photoHow sure the model isThe trained probability of that value (top 3 shown). Not a measured accuracy.
ceramic (CLIP)Is it pottery?CLIP's ceramic score, 0–1; objects below 0.35 are not selected by default.
scoreHow close a recipe isWeighted sum of the parts below, 0–1. Only the parts you gave count; their weights are scaled to add up to 1.
ΔE00How different two colours lookCIEDE2000 colour difference (made to follow human eyes). 0 = the same.
colour partColour closenessexp(−ΔE00 / 20), see the table below.
words / photo / formula partHow well the recipe fits(cosine similarity + 1) / 2 in the smart model's shared space.
learned matchWords ↔ chemistryColour match model: (cosine + 1) / 2 between the words and the recipe's chemistry.
cone · surfaceRight firing? right finish?1 when it matches (cone ranges overlap; 04 ≠ 4), else 0.
familyA chemistry groupK-Means group. Explore formulations takes at most 2 per family, to show different recipes for a similar look.
✓ / ✗ / ?Matches or notShape: same form. Glaze: same surface group (glossy / satin / matte). Colour: ΔE ≤ 20. Strict: all three. ? = no label.
Hit@KAny good one near the top?Yes if at least one of the first K results matches.
P@KHow many good ones?Matching results among the first K, divided by K.
Recall@KFound all of them?Share of all matching items that reach the top K. Shown for the true recipe ID, and in the model tests (Recall@10 = the right recipe in the top 10).
nDCG@KBest ones first?0–1; 1 = the best possible order (graded by your priority).
Hit Rate@KOver many searchesShare of searches with Hit@K = yes (📊 Scores page).
ΔE00colour partwhat it looks like
01.00the same colour
20.90hard to see the difference
50.78a small difference side by side
100.61a clearly different shade
200.37a different colour (the limit of a colour match in the scores)

10 · Photo + words + formula together

Yes, you can give all three in one search. On 🧪 Glaze recipes tick what to use (text, colour, photo object, formula). Each part has a weight: words 0.35, photo 0.35, formula 0.25, colour 0.30, cone 0.10, surface 0.10, transparency 0.05, atmosphere 0.05. Only the parts you give count, and their weights are divided by their sum, so they always add up to 1:

You giveWeights used
only a formula (example F)formula 1.00
photo + colour (example A, step 2)photo 0.54 · colour 0.46
words with colour, cone, surface, atmosphere (example E)words 0.39 · colour 0.33 · cone 0.11 · surface 0.11 · atmosphere 0.06
photo + colour + words with cone and surface (example A, step 3)words 0.29 · photo 0.29 · colour 0.25 · cone 0.08 · surface 0.08

So one input alone gets all the weight, and several inputs share it in fixed proportions. On 🏺 Similar pottery the same idea holds: photo 0.40, words 0.35, formula 0.25 when given; the sliders split the photo part between shape, glaze and colour.

11 · Tips and problems

If…Then…
the colour is the bare clay or a shadowOn 📷 My photo switch to 🎨 Pick colour and click on the glaze; or click another colour chip in What the app found.
the wrong pot is usedClick the pot you mean (yellow outline = the one in use).
the surface guess looks wrongIt often is (45 % right first): type the surface (e.g. satin) in the recipe words, or choose it in Surface.
results ignore your coneChoose it in Firing cone; remember cone 04 (low fire) is not cone 4 (mid fire).
no recipe photosThey come from Glazy: check the internet. The search itself still works.
“the formula is not used”Give at least 3 oxides including a flux (CaO, K2O, Na2O, MgO, ZnO, …).
the page says the server is not runningStart RUN_GLAZE_SEARCH.bat again and keep its window open.
a recipe looks perfectOpen it with View on Glazy and read it there; test-fire a small tile before you mix a big batch.
